item.text:
**7B.1 Research Note: Bongbong Marcos (2024)**

Best read: **mixed, leaning negative on truthfulness under reputational pressure**. I found some clearly accurate or candid public statements, but also direct independent evidence that he gave an **inaccurate / incomplete explanation** on a high-salience issue like rice inflation, plus at least one **self-aggrandizing overstatement** in Basilan. I did **not** find a strong 2024 court- or legislature-specific falsehood case in the accessible material; the evidence base here is mostly speeches, media interviews, and fact-checks.

| Title | Publisher | Date | Claim-level summary | QIDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|
| [Sona 2024 fact check](https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/1964296/sona-2024-fact-check) | Philippine Daily Inquirer | 2024-07-23 | **Negative:** Marcos’s claim that market forces alone were driving rice prices was rated **inaccurate**; the fact-check says government policy and intervention also mattered. This is the strongest evidence I found of misleading framing on a core domestic issue. | 7B.1 |
| [Sona 2024 fact check](https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/1964296/sona-2024-fact-check) | Philippine Daily Inquirer | 2024-07-23 | **Positive:** The same fact-check rated his claim about palay output exceeding 20 million metric tons as **correct**. This is evidence that some of his checkable public claims were accurate. | 7B.1 |
| [Marcos opens 2024 SONA admitting rice prices are costly](https://www.gmanetwork.com/news/topstories/nation/914278/marcos-opens-2024-sona-admitting-rice-prices-are-costly/story/) | GMA News Online | 2024-07-22 | **Positive:** Marcos publicly acknowledged that good aggregate statistics meant little to families facing expensive rice. This is candid, reality-based messaging rather than denial or spin. | 7B.1 |
| [President Ferdinand Marcos not first Philippine leader to visit strife-torn Basilan province](https://factcheck.afp.com/doc.afp.com.34M94K7) | AFP Philippines | 2024-04-02 | **Negative / weakly negative:** Marcos’s “first president to be able to come here” remark was overstated when generalized to Basilan as a whole; AFP found earlier presidents had visited the province. This is a small but real example of embellishment. | 7B.1 |
| [Philippines' Marcos has no plans to grant U.S. access to more bases](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/philippine-president-trilateral-agreement-with-us-japan-not-directed-at-anyone-3377518) | Reuters | 2024-04-15 | **Positive:** Marcos publicly said there were no plans for more U.S. bases / EDCA sites, and the report frames that as his stated position after the trilateral summit. I found no contradiction in the same reporting set. | 7B.1; 2B.7 |
| [Philippines needs to 'do more' than protest China's actions in South China Sea, Marcos says](https://theprint.in/world/philippines-needs-to-do-more-than-protest-chinas-actions-in-south-china-sea-marcos-says/2149370/) | Reuters / ThePrint | 2024-06-27 | **Positive:** Marcos publicly distinguished the June 17 maritime clash from an “armed attack” and urged more than protest, while the article also notes China disputed the Philippine account. This reads as restrained crisis communication rather than obvious fabrication. | 7B.1; 2B.7 |

**Gap**
- I did not find, in this limited search window, a clean 2024 example of Marcos lying to the legislature or courts.
- The strongest evidence is about **public messaging**: one major inaccurate framing on rice inflation, some accurate statements, and several restrained foreign-policy statements that were not obviously contradicted.

**Bottom line**
- The record does **not** support a clean “habitually tells the truth” finding.
- It does support a **mixed** read: he can make accurate and candid statements, but he also appears willing to use **selective or incomplete framing** on issues that affect reputation and political standing.
